name: Eliada
overview: Eliada is a male figure from the tribe of Judah, known primarily as a son of King David. His identity is grounded in his lineage as a member of David's family, as recorded in the Scriptures. There are no additional notes or distinctive attributes associated with him beyond his tribal affiliation and paternal relationship.
namesAndTitles: The name Eliada means 'G-d knows,' reflecting the Hebrew elements 'El' for God and a verb indicating knowledge. This proper name, recorded in 2 Samuel 5:16, does not have a special title but carries a meaningful theophoric significance common in biblical names.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Eliada as a son of David, establishing his place within the royal family. No other family relationships are recorded beyond this paternal connection.
scriptureSignificance: Eliada's significance lies in his role as one of King David's sons, contributing to the genealogical record that supports the Messianic lineage through Judah. Though not a prominent figure in narrative events, his inclusion affirms the historical and theological continuity of David's family line as presented in the biblical text.
